cases.name: bind-checkpoint-push-remote-log-equals-ours
cases.notes: §5.12 "The remote binding" / "Push" (17.6, Phase 6b). The repository is born disabled, `history enable --provider git` baselines two documents; `history remote set --url <remote>` (the case's second bare repository, a local path — no network; `name` origin, the remote branch the local one, push and fetch `off` — nothing is automatic until configured) writes the row's `remote` member and the git remote; `remote status` before any push is `unknown` (no remote tip known). An edit and a checkpoint, then `history push`: the branch AND the ids ref go over (`ids: pushed`), `pushed_through` is the tip's `omgbase-seq` (4), the remote's log — `git log --format=%H%n%s%n%(trailers)` on the remote — is byte for byte ours, status `in-sync`. `git_ids_show` on the REMOTE lists d_0's id map from a clone of both refs: canonical JSON `{ blocks: [{ hash, id, ordinal, parent }], doc, head }` with the ids the reconcile minted (the heading kept b_0, the edited paragraph is b_4) and the head r_2. `remote unset` removes the binding; a push without one is the pinned refusal.

cases.name: push-on-checkpoint-and-the-rejected-push
cases.notes: §5.12 "Push": `push: on-checkpoint` runs the push after every checkpoint that committed — the receipt carries `push: { pushed, tip, pushed_through, ids }`; a checkpoint with nothing to commit pushes nothing (no `push` member). Then someone else commits on the remote (`git_remote_commit`: identity `remote <remote@fixture>`, the step's `ts`) and we checkpoint a local edit: the push is REJECTED (non-fast-forward) — never forced — the `git_remote_diverged` alert is raised (warning; detail `{ remote, branch, local_tip, remote_tip }`, no `old_remote_tip`: a rejection pauses nothing) and the receipt's `push.error` is the pinned message; `alerts` shows it; `remote status` reads `diverged`. A `history fetch` merges the remote's commit (both sides moved: one merge commit with `omgbase-merge`), the alert is gone, and the next push lands: the remote's log is ours again.

cases.name: fetch-fast-forwards-through-the-source-boundary
cases.notes: §5.12 "Fetch" — the remote ahead, we not: `git_remote_commit` edits a.md and adds c.md on the remote after our push; `history fetch` writes the two files into the vault THROUGH THE SOURCE BOUNDARY (the fixture's sink is `observeBatch`: the ordinary reconcile matches a.md's identity — d_0 keeps its id, the heading keeps b_0 — and the feed records two observed rows, c_3 and c_4), then fast-forwards our branch to the remote's tip (a commit that is not the worker's: no trailers). The checkpoint that follows finds the rows' bytes already in the tree and COMMITS NOTHING (`committed 0`, the tip unchanged, the cursor advanced to seq 5 — the no-op rule) while the ids ref records the new heads (`git_ids_log`: an ids commit at seq 4-5 whose `omgbase-content` is the remote's tip; `git_ids_show` lists d_2, the new document). `docs` shows a.md's bytes as the remote wrote them; status `in-sync`.

cases.name: both-sides-moved-conflict-sidecar-alert-resolve
cases.notes: §5.12 "Merge" — a CONFLICT: both sides edited a.md to different bytes. `history fetch` keeps both versions: ours stays at a.md, the remote's is written into the vault as `a.remote-<short sha>.md` beside it (a document like any other — the `docs` projection lists it), the `git_merge_conflict` alert is raised (warning; detail `{ remote, branch, remote_tip, paths, base }`), and NO merge commit is made (the tip is ours). A second fetch and a push refuse while the conflict stands; the checkpoint commits the sidecar as a document of the vault. `history remote resolve a.md --theirs` writes the remote's bytes over a.md, removes the sidecar, and — the last conflict settled — checkpoints the resolution and writes the merge commit over it (parents: our tip, the remote's tip); the alert is gone; the push lands.

cases.name: rewritten-remote-detect-stop-alert
cases.notes: §5.12 "Divergence" — the default: detect, stop, alert. After our push the remote gains a commit (c.md) we fetch (fast-forward) and push past; then the remote is REWRITTEN — `git_remote_commit` with `parent: tip^` replaces that commit (a rebase / force-push: c.md's other version and d.md on top of the commit before). We checkpoint an unpushed local edit. `history fetch` sees the remote's tip does not descend from the tip we last knew: `{ state: diverged }`, the `git_remote_diverged` alert (warning; detail `{ remote, branch, local_tip, remote_tip, old_remote_tip }`), the old tip kept on `refs/omgbase/diverged/origin`; push and fetch now refuse with the pinned message; `reconcile` on a repository that is NOT diverged (step 7, before the fetch) refuses too; a checkpoint still commits locally. Nothing was force-pushed: the remote's log is its own.

cases.name: rewritten-remote-reconcile-adopt
cases.notes: §5.12 "Divergence" — `--adopt`: the remote's head becomes truth. Its tree is written into the vault through the source boundary: c.md (changed on the remote alone since the old tip) takes the remote's bytes; a.md — edited HERE since the last agreement and not on the remote — surfaces as a conflict: the remote's (old) bytes take the path and ours stay beside it as `a.local-<short sha of our tip>.md`; the `git_merge_conflict` alert names the path with `holds: ours`. Our branch is reset to the remote's tip, our previous tip kept on `refs/omgbase/backup/20261020T100700Z`. The checkpoint that follows commits the sidecar on top of the adopted head (the adopted paths are no-ops). `resolve a.md --ours` brings our edit back to the path and drops the sidecar — no merge commit is pending here (`merged: null`).
